bullets.text: Q2 CR 92.6 was strong and in-line with seasonal expectations; investment portfolio achieved 5.5% total return; company achieved acceptable profit margins and small positive written and earned premium growth.

Capital position stands comfortably over $1B above regulatory capital and extreme contingency load; portfolio derisked for downside protection; accounting guidance reclassified non-credit impairments to unrealized losses without affecting shareholders’ equity.

Personal Lines PIF grew 4% year-over-year, approaching 11 million policies. Special lines PIF increased at low single digits, partly through renewals. Strong consumer shopping behavior and demand continued through the second quarter.

Direct written premium grew 9% for the quarter and year. Agency new business sales finished strong near quarter-end, channel premium growth approached flat, and agency competitiveness appeared to increase modestly.

Personal Injury Protection (PIP) losses escalated seriously in key states, causing considerable angst. Outside PIP, aggregate severity trends were less remarkable. Claims frequency and process restructuring allowed settling claims at believed reduced costs.
Management expects aggregate trends to be more rate positive than negative. Rate needs have generally been approved in a timely manner, and rate changes are implemented or planned in most PIP states.

Progressive resized Claims management infrastructure and reduced its Claims workforce by about 2%. Policies in force per employee equivalent continued strengthening through process design, increased retention, and Internet-based self-service.

Net premium growth remained positive primarily from unit growth amid negative-to-low average premium-per-policy trends; Commercial Auto new business sales declined, though the rate of decline slowed during Q2.
'Name Your Price' program rolled out nationwide during Q2 following nearly a year of test marketing, delivering pleasing results and an improved consumer experience in the Direct channel.

Economic malaise dampened motorcycle sales, but usage and loss results matched seasonal expectations. In agent quoting, price transparency makes competitive positioning changes rapid and increases penalties for pricing inaccuracies.
